input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle guard was removed from the walk over the __cause__ chain, so a cyclic chain now loops forever.
- rationale: Trigger: a retried call raises an exception whose __cause__ chain forms a cycle (e.g., a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, which Python allows when assigned manually), and no exception in the cycle matches exception_cause_types. Mechanism: the while loop on line 180 never reaches None and never hits the seen-set break that was just deleted, so each iteration keeps following the cycle. Impact: the retry decision never returns, so the calling thread hangs instead of retrying or raising.
critique: Both describe the same defect: the walk over __cause__ has no cycle guard, so a self-referential or mutual chain never reaches None and the retry predicate loops forever, hanging the caller. The trigger, mechanism and impact are the same.
